question: A 50-year-old man comes to the emergency department for evaluation of right-sided facial weakness that he noticed after waking up. One month ago, he also experienced right-sided neck pain and headache that began after returning from a hunting trip to New Hampshire the week before. He took ibuprofen to relieve symptoms, which subsided a week later. He has a 5-year history of hypertension controlled with drug therapy. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years and he drinks two beers daily. His vital signs are within the normal range. Physical examination shows right-sided drooping of the upper and lower half of the face. The patient has difficulties smiling and he is unable to close his right eye. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

options.opb: Polymerase chain reaction of the facial skin

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: History of right-sided facial weakness -> Physical examination findings of right-sided drooping of the face -> Suggestive of facial nerve palsy -> 80% CHAIN: History of right-sided neck pain and headache after a hunting trip -> Possible exposure to tick bites in New Hampshire -> Concern for Lyme disease -> 70% CHAIN: History of hypertension and smoking -> Increased risk for vascular events -> Consider cerebrovascular etiology for facial weakness -> 60% CHAIN: Physical examination findings of inability to close the right eye -> Suggestive of facial nerve involvement -> Consider facial nerve pathology -> 70% CHAIN: Physical examination findings of normal vital signs -> Excludes acute life-threatening conditions -> Allows for further diagnostic workup -> 80%
analysis: Given the patient's presentation of right-sided facial weakness following a trip to an area where Lyme disease is endemic, coupled with the history of neck pain and headache, the most appropriate next step in diagnosis would be to test for Lyme disease.
